0.text: Abs show once body fat drops to roughly 12 to 15% for most men, and you're at 22.8% now, so this is really a body fat goal: at a safe pace that's around 6 to 8 kg of fat, which takes about 4 to 5 months. By when would you like to get there?

Congratulations! 14 Feb is about 15 weeks away, and at a safe pace of around 0.6 to 0.8 kg a week you could be roughly 9 to 11 kg lighter than your 81.9 kg by then. What weight would you like to be on the day?

20 kg in 2 months would mean losing about 2.5 kg a week, which is much faster than is safe; I suggest at most about 0.8 kg a week at your weight. At that pace 20 kg takes about 6 months, so roughly early May 2027. Shall I set 62 kg by 5 May as your goal?

Good on you for starting. The simplest start is to pick one goal with a date, then for the first couple of weeks just log every meal and get your daily walk in; strength training comes in once that's a habit. What would you like to change about your body, and by when?

That's a great reason to start, and you don't need a number for it. Feeling less tired usually comes down to sleep, moving every day and eating enough protein at regular meals, and logging your meals here is the easiest way to see which one is off. If you'd like something to measure, would a target weight or body fat % with a date help, or would you rather just start with the habits?

Very doable: the aim is a lean gain, so a small surplus of about 300 kcal a day, plenty of protein from dal, paneer, curd and soya, and strength training 3 days a week. At a steady 0.25 to 0.5 kg a week, 8 kg takes about 4 to 8 months. Would you like 66 kg by around June as your goal?

At 176 cm, 55 kg would put you under a healthy weight (a BMI around 17.8), so I wouldn't aim that low. A healthy range for your height is roughly 62 to 75 kg. What's drawing you to 55, is it a look or a number you have in mind?

That level of physique takes years of training and a very low body fat, so 3 months won't get you there, but it can make a real visible difference. At your current pace 3 months is about 7 kg down from 81.9 kg with your strength going up, which will show in your face, waist and arms. Want to keep building towards that look with your 74 kg goal as the first step?

Love that. A 10k by March is very doable if you build up gradually: run 2 to 3 times a week, adding a little distance each week, and keep your 3 gym days for strength. Which days would suit your runs, so I can add them to your routine?

That makes sense, and it's a good shift: keep protein high at 120 g or more, train with progressive overload, and eat close to maintenance, so the scale moves slower but your body changes. Would you like to set a body fat % target with a date, say around 18%, instead of the 74 kg weight goal?

From 81.9 to 74 kg by 31 Jan is about 0.6 kg a week over 13 weeks, which you're on pace for right now. Day to day that means staying under 1800 kcal with at least 120 g of protein, 8000 steps, and the gym on Mon, Wed and Fri. Protein is your most missed check this week, so that's the one to focus on first.
Keep this first week simple: log every meal, even roughly, and get your daily walk in. You've logged every day so far, which is exactly the habit that makes the rest work.

Looking toned is mostly a bit less fat plus some muscle, so strength training 3 days a week and getting your 95 g of protein matter more than the scale. Would you like to switch your goal from weight to a body fat target, say around 28% by end of January?

6 kg in 3 weeks isn't safe, and most of it would be water that comes straight back; about 2 kg is realistic. What will show most in 3 weeks is less bloating from cutting back on salt and fried food, hitting your protein, daily steps and good sleep before the day.

That's very common, and it's usually about what's within reach rather than willpower. Try not keeping the big packets at home, or buy small single packs and keep them out of sight, and have roasted chana or makhana ready for when you want something crunchy at night.

Once you're home the couch wins, so the trick is not going home first: pack your gym bag the night before and go straight from office. Would it help to move your gym slot earlier, closer to when you leave work?

That's really common, and it usually means the start was too big to keep up. Pick a smaller version you can do even on a bad day, like logging one line and a 15-minute walk, and keep one rule: never miss two days in a row. Your on-track days are the number to watch, not perfect weeks.

Tie it to the meal itself: snap a photo of your plate before you start eating, and log it from the photo when you're done. Even one rough line is enough, and the meal reminders can nudge you if you turn them on.

5 pm is when hunger peaks, so plan for it: carry a snack from home for 4:30, like a fruit, roasted chana or a glass of buttermilk, and you'll find the samosa much easier to skip. Having one now and then is fine, just log it.

The midnight snacking is mostly the late night itself: you're awake and hungry long after dinner. Pick a kitchen-closed time and brush your teeth after dinner as the signal, and try moving bedtime 15 minutes earlier each week.

That's a mother's love, and it's tricky to refuse. Try telling her about your goal and asking for extra sabzi or dal instead of the extra roti, or serve your own plate before she does, with a little ghee on the side rather than on top.

Weekends don't undo your weekdays, they just slow things down. Plan one meal out on the weekend and keep the rest close to normal, and a Saturday morning walk helps the whole day stay on track. If you know you're eating out, tell me beforehand and I'll help you plan it.

Make it easier than snoozing: keep your shoes and clothes by the bed and put the alarm across the room so you have to get up. Start with just 10 minutes; once you're out the door, it's usually easy to keep going.

Keep dal, paneer or tofu, curd, sprouts, seasonal fruit and roasted chana or makhana stocked, so the easy option is the good one. Keep fried snacks and biscuits out of the house, since what's at home is what gets eaten.

You didn't ruin anything: one big meal doesn't undo weeks of good days, it's a blip on the scale for a day or two. Just eat your next meal as normal, no skipping to make up for it. Want me to log the pizza for last night?

I get it, breaking a streak feels bad, but it doesn't erase what you built. You had a solid stretch from 24 to 29 Oct, and you're back today, which is what counts. Let's just make today a good day and not miss twice.

Motivation comes and goes, so don't rely on it; rely on the routine: the gym at fixed times on Mon, Wed and Fri, meals logged, and a daily walk. Watch your on-track days each week rather than the scale, because they show progress first. What's the main reason you want to reach 74 kg by January?

Out of sight really is out of mind: pass a few boxes on to neighbours or the office and keep the rest in a cupboard, not on the table. Plan one piece after a meal on the days you want it, enjoy it, and log it.
Serve your plate in the kitchen and leave the serving dishes there, so you're not reaching for seconds while watching. Once the plate is done, so is dinner.
Keep a filled bottle on your desk and have a glass with each meal, so it happens without thinking. Tell me how much you drink and I'll log it.
